title: Photo-Based Mission Design
subtitle: Honor of Kings: World
summary: Designed a mission mode within the existing photo system, specifying activation, target checks, and exit behavior.
description: Mission photography needed familiar photo controls alongside task-specific success checks. I documented the flow, selected the features to reuse, and coordinated with mission designers, programmers, and the production team.
ownership: Defined the mission photo mode with a mentor, documented requirements and flow, and coordinated with mission designers, programmers, and the production team.
Specified activation, task and target display, photo checks, success handling, and exit behavior.
Defined a feature allowlist and reused the existing recognition, occlusion checks, and event-editor capabilities.
evidence: Activation, target checks, and exit handling for mission photography.

sections.title: A mission mode within the existing photo system
sections.intro: The regular photo system already had many features. Inheriting all of them would add unnecessary cases, while building a separate system would duplicate maintenance.
paragraphs: I treated mission photography as a special mode within the existing system. It retained the existing controls and programming capabilities, with a feature allowlist defining what the mode could use.
This let us reuse the system while documenting task-specific target display, success checks, and completion behavior separately, without extending every regular photo feature to mission use.

sections.title: Activation, target checks, and exit handling

points.title: Activation
points.text: Activate mission mode based on the tracked mission and its configured trigger area. Skip the area check if the mission has no assigned area.

points.title: Targets and capture
points.text: Display the current task and targets in photo mode. On capture, use existing recognition and occlusion checks to determine completion.

points.title: Completion and exit
points.text: Define success, failure, and exit handling separately, including preventing another capture after the task succeeds.

sections.title: Removing unnecessary capture restrictions
sections.intro: We initially considered limits on distance, angle, frame position, and target size. We ultimately kept only the occlusion requirement.
paragraphs: Those limits would require extra rules for different camera positions and more implementation work. I focused the checks on whether the target was captured effectively, using the existing recognition and occlusion checks.
I documented edge cases in flow diagrams, confirmed their handling during reviews, and checked the implementation with the production team.

outcomes: Delivered the flow and requirements for mission photography, including feature reuse and handling for success, failure, and exit.
